sections.title: Q4 and FY 2025 Update
sections.summary: This section serves as the title page and table of contents for the 'Q4 and FY 2025 Update' presentation. It outlines the document's structure, listing key sections such as Highlights, Financial Summary, Operational Summary, Manufacturing & Hardware, AI & Software, Services, Outlook, and Key Metrics, along with their corresponding page numbers.

sections.title: HIGHLIGHTS
sections.summary: The 'HIGHLIGHTS' section outlines key financial and operational achievements for 2025. Under Profitability, it lists GAAP operating income of $4.4B, net income of $3.8B, and non-GAAP net income of $5.9B. The Cash section details an operating cash flow of $14.7B, free cash flow of $6.2B, and a total cash and investments balance of $44.1B. Operational highlights include the removal of safety monitors from Robotaxis in Austin, record energy storage deployments, and record vehicle deliveries in APAC.

sections.title: SUMMARY
sections.summary: The 'SUMMARY' section outlines Tesla's strategic transition in 2025 from a hardware-centric business to a physical AI company. Key achievements include advancing Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology, launching the Robotaxi service, and initiating production lines for Cybercab and Optimus robots. The text details the company's system-level approach to autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots, emphasizing vertical integration and cost optimization. It also highlights the refresh of the vehicle lineup with the new Model Y and the evolution of energy offerings. Looking ahead to 2026, the summary notes plans to invest in infrastructure for clean energy and transport, including the ramp-up of six new production lines across various manufacturing sectors.

sections.title: FINANCIAL SUMMARY
sections.summary: The section titled 'FINANCIAL SUMMARY' presents two comprehensive tables of unaudited financial data. The first table details quarterly performance metrics for the fiscal year 2024 and 2025 (Q4-2024 through Q4-2025), while the second table provides annual historical data from 2021 to 2025. Both tables report figures in millions of dollars, excluding percentages and per share data. Key metrics tracked include revenue breakdowns by segment (automotive, energy generation/storage, services), total revenues, gross profit, operating expenses, income from operations, adjusted EBITDA, net income (GAAP and non-GAAP), earnings per share (EPS), and cash flow indicators such as capital expenditures and free cash flow.

sections.title: OPERATIONAL SUMMARY
sections.summary: The 'OPERATIONAL SUMMARY' section presents two tables detailing Tesla's operational metrics. The first table provides quarterly data from Q4 2024 through Q4 2025, while the second table offers annual historical data from 2021 to 2025. Key metrics tracked include vehicle production (broken down by Model 3/Y and other models), deliveries (including total, subject to operating lease accounting, and cumulative all-time figures), Active FSD Subscriptions, end-of-period operating lease counts, global vehicle inventory days of supply, storage deployed in GWh, Tesla locations, and Supercharger infrastructure (stations and connectors).

children.title: Automotive
children.summary: The section discusses automotive sales performance, noting a sequential decline but an improvement in gross margin and strong results in the APAC region. It details the rollout of Model Y variants and preparations for future production ramps of Tesla Semi, Cybercab, and the next-generation Roadster. The accompanying table outlines installed annual manufacturing capacity across various regions (California, Shanghai, Berlin, Texas, Nevada) for products including Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Tesla Semi.

children.title: Energy generation and storage
children.summary: The section details record quarterly energy storage deployments driven by Megapack, resulting in a record gross profit of $1.1 billion. It outlines plans to begin production of Megapack 3 and Megablock at the Megafactory Houston in 2026. Additionally, it notes that the global Powerwall network supported over 89,000 Virtual Power Plant events across more than 1 million units in 2025. The accompanying table lists installed annual manufacturing capacity for Energy Generation and Storage products (Megapack, Powerwall) across regions including California, Nevada, Shanghai, and Texas.

children.title: Robotics
children.summary: The Robotics section details progress on the Optimus program in 2025, specifically the unveiling of the Gen 3 version with major upgrades and a new hand design intended for mass production. It outlines plans to start production before the end of 2026 with an eventual capacity of 1 million robots per year. The accompanying table indicates that the Optimus robot is currently under construction in California.

children.title: AI Training Compute
children.summary: The section details the construction of Cortex 2 at Gigafactory Texas to increase AI training compute capacity, with plans to more than double onsite compute in terms of H100 equivalents by the first half of 2026. The accompanying table outlines installed annual capacity for AI Training Compute, listing 'Cortex 1' in Texas as having over 100k H100e capacity in production and 'Cortex 2' under construction.

children.title: Battery
children.summary: The section details the company's battery manufacturing progress, including the commencement of pilot production at its lithium refinery in North America (the first spodumene-to-lithium hydroxide facility). It also covers the production of 4680 cells and battery packs for Model Ys using dry-electrode technology made in Austin. The text notes expectations for domestic cathode material production in Texas and LFP lines in Nevada to begin in 2026.

children.title: Other Supporting Infrastructure
children.summary: This section outlines the company's strategy for supporting infrastructure, focusing on the efficient utilization of its North American physical footprint to support the Robotaxi rollout. It details plans to augment existing charging networks, service centers, and sales locations as demand grows, specifically noting the addition of over 3,800 new Supercharging stalls.

children.title: AI Software
children.summary: The section details the enhancement of FSD (Supervised) version v14, an end-to-end foundation model trained on customer and Robotaxi data. It highlights safety features like autonomous parking and accessibility for those with difficulty driving. The text also mentions the global fleet's ability to collect over 500 years of continuous driving data daily to handle corner cases.

children.title: AI Inference Compute
children.summary: The section details the development of in-house AI5 and AI6 inference chips for autonomy, with production planned for 2027 and 2028. It highlights a targeted 50x performance improvement for the AI5 chip over the AI4, driven by a 10x increase in raw compute, 9x memory capacity, and 5x hardened block quantization and softmax function.

children.title: Automotive and Other Software
children.summary: This section details recent software updates and features for Tesla vehicles, including the removal of waitlists for the Robotaxi iOS app. It highlights over-the-air enhancements such as Grok AI companion support for navigation commands, Tesla Photobooth for in-car photography, Supercharger Site Maps with live availability, Automatic HOV Lane Routing based on camera occupancy detection, a Phone Left Behind Chime, and the SpaceX ISS Docking Simulator Game.

children.title: Robotaxi
children.summary: The section details the progress of driverless Robotaxi services, including testing in Austin starting in December and removing safety monitors in January. It also mentions the launch of Bay Area ride-hailing service at San Jose Airport in October. The section includes a chart showing cumulative paid Robotaxi miles projected through December 2025 and a table outlining planned coverage for various US states (California, Texas, Arizona, Florida, Nevada) with specific metro areas and expected status or launch dates.

children.title: FSD (Supervised)
children.summary: The section details the launch and growth of FSD (Supervised) in South Korea, where customers drove over 1 million kilometers in one month. It mentions ongoing regulatory pursuits in China and Europe and ride-along experiences in Italy, Germany, France, and Switzerland. Additionally, it notes that monthly subscriptions for the service more than doubled in 2025 and that access is transitioning to a monthly subscription model only.

children.title: Automotive Services
children.summary: The section details the performance of 'Services and Other' gross profit, which was approximately $300 million, driven by Part Sales and Supercharging. It highlights the expansion of Tesla Insurance to Florida and explains a discount program where customers using FSD (Supervised) receive reduced insurance premiums.

sections.title: OTHER UPDATES
sections.summary: This page details an agreement reached on January 16, 2026, where Tesla invested approximately $2 billion to acquire Series E Preferred Stock of xAI. The text explains that this investment is part of Tesla's Master Plan Part IV and includes a framework agreement to evaluate potential AI collaborations between the two companies. The transaction is subject to regulatory conditions with an expected closing in Q1'2026.

children.title: Volume
children.summary: The section outlines the company's focus on maximizing factory capacity utilization. It notes that deliveries and deployments depend on aggregate demand, supply chain readiness, and allocation decisions between customer sales and use in the company's own fleet.

children.title: Cash
children.summary: The section outlines the company's strategy to maintain a strong balance sheet and sufficient liquidity. This financial management approach is intended to fund the product roadmap, long-term capacity expansion plans (including vertical integration), and other expenses.

children.title: Profit
children.summary: The section outlines the company's strategy to reduce manufacturing and operational costs through innovation. It states that over time, hardware-related profits are expected to be supplemented by an acceleration of profits from AI, software, and fleet-based services.

children.title: Product
children.summary: The section outlines the company's strategy to evolve its product lineup with a focus on cost, scale, and monetization via AI software. It emphasizes growing sales volumes by optimizing existing production capacity before building new facilities. Additionally, it provides specific timelines for volume production: Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 are scheduled to start in 2026, while first-generation production lines for Optimus are currently being installed.

sections.title: PHOTOS & CHARTS
sections.summary: This section presents a series of images highlighting Tesla's vehicle safety ratings and autonomous driving capabilities. It features the Model Y, recognized as the 2025 best-in-class small SUV by Euro NCAP, and the Model 3, recognized as the 2025 best-in-class large family car by Euro NCAP. The section also showcases Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) V14 software, which offers driver assistance, and documents the testing phase of the Driverless Robotaxi in Austin.

sections.title: TESLA SEMI - MEGACHARGER NETWORK PLANNED SITES FOR 2026
sections.path: TSLA-Q4-2025-Update.pdf/TESLA SEMI - MEGACHARGER NETWORK PLANNED SITES FOR 2026
sections.summary: The section displays a map of the United States illustrating the planned locations for Tesla Semi Megacharger network sites in 2026. Red markers indicate the specific cities and regions where these charging stations are scheduled to be built.

sections.title: KEY METRICS QUARTERLY
sections.summary: This page displays quarterly key metrics for a company, presented as three bar charts covering the period from 1Q-2023 to 4Q-2025. The first chart shows Vehicle Deliveries in millions of units, while the second and third charts display financial performance including Operating Cash Flow, Free Cash Flow, Net Income, and Adjusted EBITDA in billions of dollars. The data is marked as Unaudited.

sections.title: KEY METRICS TRAILING 12 MONTHS (TTM)
sections.summary: The page displays a set of three bar charts titled 'KEY METRICS TRAILING 12 MONTHS (TTM)' showing financial and operational data from Q1 2023 through Q4 2025. The first chart tracks Vehicle Deliveries in millions of units, the second compares Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow in billions of dollars, and the third contrasts Net Income with Adjusted EBITDA, also in billions.

children.title: Revenue
children.summary: The section details that total quarterly revenue decreased 3% year-over-year to $24.9 billion. It lists the factors impacting this change, including decreases in vehicle deliveries and regulatory credit revenue, offset by growth in Energy Generation and Storage, Services and Other, positive foreign exchange impact, and higher average selling prices.

children.title: Profitability
children.summary: The Profitability section details a 11% year-over-year decrease in quarterly operating income to $1.4 billion, resulting in a 5.7% operating margin. The decline was primarily driven by increased SBC and restructuring charges, higher operating expenses related to AI and R&D projects, and an increase in average cost per vehicle due to lower fixed cost absorption and tariffs. These negative factors were partially offset by growth in gross profit from Energy Generation and Storage, Services and Other, and other automotive ancillary sales.

sections.title: FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
sections.summary: This page serves as a section divider or title page for the financial statements. It features a minimalist black background with the text 'FINANCIAL STATEMENTS' centered in white capital letters. The Tesla logo is visible in the bottom right corner.

sections.title: STATEMENT OF OPERATIONS
sections.summary: The page displays an Unaudited Statement of Operations for a company, detailing financial performance across five quarters from Q4-2024 to Q4-2025. The table is structured into sections covering Revenues (Automotive sales, Energy generation, Services), Cost of Revenues, Operating Expenses, and Net Income. Key columns include Total revenues, Gross profit, Income from operations, and Net income attributable to common stockholders, with figures presented in millions of USD.

sections.title: BALANCE SHEET
sections.summary: The page displays an Unaudited Balance Sheet for a company, presenting financial data in millions of USD across five quarterly periods from December 31, 2024, to December 31, 2025. The table details Assets (including current assets like cash and inventory, and non-current assets such as property and digital assets), Liabilities (current and long-term debt, accounts payable), and Equity. Key totals show Total Assets increasing from 122,070 million to 137,806 million over the period.

sections.title: STATEMENT OF CASH FLOWS
sections.summary: The page displays an Unaudited Statement of Cash Flows, presenting financial data in millions of USD across five quarters from Q4-2024 to Q4-2025. The table details cash flows categorized into operating activities (including net income and adjustments like depreciation), investing activities (such as capital expenditures and investment purchases), and financing activities (including debt activities and vehicle financing). It concludes with the net increase or decrease in cash and the ending cash balance for each period.

sections.title: RECONCILIATION OF GAAP TO NON-GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION
sections.path: TSLA-Q4-2025-Update.pdf/RECONCILIATION OF GAAP TO NON-GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION
sections.summary: The section titled 'RECONCILIATION OF GAAP TO NON-GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION' presents a series of financial tables detailing the reconciliation between Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and non-GAAP metrics. The data is provided in millions of USD, with per-share data where applicable, covering quarterly periods from Q2 2022 through Q4 2025 and annual periods from 2021 to 2025. Key metrics reconciled include Net Income attributable to common stockholders, Earnings Per Share (EPS), Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow, and Automotive Gross Margin. The tables show adjustments for items such as stock-based compensation, digital assets gains/losses, interest expense, taxes, and regulatory credit revenue.

children.title: WEBCAST INFORMATION
children.summary: The section provides details regarding a live webcast of Tesla's fourth quarter 2025 financial results conference call. It specifies the start time as 4:30 p.m. CT on January 28, 2026, and notes that the event will be available at ir.tesla.com. Additionally, it mentions that a replay of the webcast will be accessible for approximately one year.

children.title: CERTAIN TERMS
children.summary: This section defines specific terms used in the document, including vehicle deliveries, energy product deployment volume, Net income attributable to common stockholders (non-GAAP), Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP), Free cash flow, Average cost per vehicle, Days sales outstanding, Days payable outstanding, and Days of supply.

children.title: NON-GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION
children.summary: This section explains that Tesla presents consolidated financial information on both a GAAP and non-GAAP basis. It lists specific non-GAAP measures used by management, including non-GAAP net income (loss), Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, non-GAAP automotive gross margin, and free cash flow. The text states these metrics are used for internal planning and to help investors understand the company's performance, noting that they should be read in conjunction with U.S. GAAP financial information.

children.title: FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS
children.summary: This section contains a legal disclaimer regarding forward-looking statements made by Tesla. It defines these statements as those related to future expectations, strategies, and performance metrics (such as production, demand, and profitability) which are based on assumptions and involve risks and uncertainties. The text lists numerous potential factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these projections, including manufacturing delays, supply chain issues, regulatory changes, competition, and product safety. It references the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 and directs readers to SEC filings for more detailed risk information.
